memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When Moses approached the camp and saw the calf and the dancing, his anger burned and he threw the tablets out of his hands, breaking them to pieces at the foot of the mountain. And he took the calf they had made and burned it in the fire; then he ground it to powder, scattered it on the water and made the Israelites drink it." - Exod 32:19-20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses had just spent verses pleading for these people. Now he sees it with his own eyes, and he burns.

Interceding for people does not mean excusing them. Moses could plead for Israel before God and still confront Israel's sin without flinching. Real love does both.

The broken tablets are not a tantrum. They are a picture. The covenant had already been shattered by the people; Moses simply made it visible at the foot of the mountain where the covenant had been given.

Then he is thorough. Burned, ground to powder, scattered, and made them drink it. The idol they had adored became something bitter in their mouths. That is what idols ultimately do — what we crave most, when we finally get it apart from God, turns to dust on the tongue.

Notice that Moses does not merely put the calf away. He destroys it completely. When God exposes an idol in our lives, half-measures do not work. Jesus spoke about cutting off what causes us to stumble (Matt 5:29-30) — strong language for a real danger.

Is there something in your life you have been managing rather than destroying?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Can you name something you have been "managing" instead of removing?
2. Do you love people enough to tell them the truth?
3. What idol has already turned bitter in your experience?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, expose what I have been hiding, and give me courage to deal with it completely. Amen.
